:::{#exm-mvn-univariate}
#### The univariate normal is the case $p = 1$

With $p = 1$, $\vecf{\mean} = (\mean)$, and $\matr{\covmat} = (\ss)$ for $\ss > 0$,
$\det(\matr{\covmat}) = \ss$
([determinant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-determinant), $p = 1$)
and $\matr{\covmat}^{-1} = (1/\ss)$, so:

$$
\ba
\p(\vX = \vx)
&= \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{1/2} (\ss)^{1/2}}
\ef{-\frac{1}{2} (x - \mean) \frac{1}{\ss} (x - \mean)}
&& \text{(substitute into the multivariate normal density)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sdpar\sqrt{2\pi}} \ef{-\frac{(x - \mean)^2}{2\ss}}
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

which is the [normal density](random-variables.qmd#def-normal) $\ndist{\mean, \ss}$.

:::
